text_fidelity_a:
Apple AirPods Max Wireless Over-Ear Headphones. Active Noise Cancelling, Transparency Mode, Spatial Audio, Digital Crown for Volume Control. Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone - Green I see people raving up and down about the perfection and wonderfulness of these headphones; I’m not as completely blown away by them as those people are. Quality of construction does seem to be excellent (although because Amazon doesn’t lower all prices at the start of Prime Day but only lowers some of them well after Prime Day has begun, I had to send back the first pair I bought and purchase another pair to get a discounted price, and the piston things for extending and compressing the size of the headphones was smoother on the first pair I had) and they’re comfortable enough to wear for extended periods, but while it may be a limitation of Bluetooth (I don’t know), I haven’t noticed myself being amazed by their bass response. No, in fact I just now watched the video for Shake It Off and listened to a couple of Lana Del Rey tracks and these headphones are definitely lacking in bass response – as in, there’s very little, and what there is gets completely lost under any midrange and high-end sounds that may be playing at the same time. They’re tinny-sounding. I have to wonder what the people are listening to with these who are praising the sound quality so enthusiastically.

On the other hand, I don’t ordinarily listen to music anymore, but only to talks and lectures; While I’m watching movies is probably the only time I’m going to really want big bass, and I watched The Revenant last night and didn’t feel like I was missing anything…

So their construction is much more solid than that of probably most other headphones on the market, they’re comfortable to wear, and there’s a nice ecosystem of accessories out there, but I personally find the sound quality quite lacking and I’m going to have to decide whether to hang onto these or return them.
text_fidelity_b: Apple AirPods Max Wireless Over-Ear Headphones. Active Noise Cancelling, Transparency Mode, Spatial Audio, Digital Crown for Volume Control. Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone - Green

text_fidelity_a:
Sony BDP-S350 1080p Blu-Ray Disc Player I've had my Sony S350 Blu-Ray player for over a year now and here are my thoughts. The picture is completely amazing, even makes regular dvd's look better. I love that there's no more cords for picture and more cords for sound, just one HDMI cable and poof - high quality picture and surround sound.

A couple things to consider before buying your Blu-Ray player and subsequent Blu-Ray discs:
1. Blu-Ray will play your regular dvd's but if you have a regular dvd player (such as in your car) you cannot play Blu-Ray discs in it.

2. Patience is needed with this unit. After putting in a movie, especially if it is somewhat new, it could take 3-5 minutes to load. I am personally never in that much of a hurry to start the movie. While the movie is loading (a progress/status bar is provided on-screen) I can make popcorn, get the dogs situated, etc.

3. In conjunction with #2, the owner of this player must also be diligent about updating the firmware inside the player. I updated my player once last year (in November) and have noticed slower loads with current movies, so I plan to update it again next month (March). My guess is that it's good to update it 1-2 times per year.
What's involved in updating the firmware? I log onto a blu-ray firmware site, choose my model of player, then burn the update to a dvd disc. Place the disc in the player, it will read and update your firmware (took mine about 5-10 minutes as I remember). Afterward, your player will load movies more quickly.
Note: Loading never occurs during the movie, the only load-time that is experienced comes immediately after inserting the disc. Here's an example of the patience it takes to operate this blu-ray player:
Turn the player on - wait about 30 seconds for the unit to be able to receive or eject a disc (if you're trying to quickly eject a disc and run it back to the movie store, this can seem long!)
Insert disc and close - wait 3-5 minutes for movie menu to load

After that, you're set to go. For me, it's worth the wait and the trouble to keep it updated. I am quite sure that future models will require less patience and diligence, but for now this is the way it is. If you want extremely good quality with your movies, it's a wonderful addition to your home theater.
text_fidelity_b: Sony BDP-S350 1080p Blu-Ray Disc Player

Misfit Phase Hybrid Wearables Smartwatch - Rose Gold I've been wearing a smaller type fitness tracker for the past 6 months. Just started wearing this Misfit and there's a few things I don't like about it and many things I love about it.
I will start with all that I really enjoy about the Misfit. I like how easy it was to pair with my phone. Even though it sits higher than my other tracker, I like that it looks like an every day stylish watch and not like a fitness tracker. And it's very comfortable to wear. The buttons on the sides are more low keyed and not that obvious that it is a fitness tracker.
Love the sleep tracker of this smartwatch. My other tracker wasn't as good as tracking my sleep.
Step tracking is right on track with what I am walking. Very important to me.
I am still learning all the nice functions that come with this Misfit. So far I love the call notification and the alerts. Like that I can play and pause my music without taking my phone out of my pocket. I am still working on learning how to work my home smart devices using the Misfit but, I know in time, and with practice, I will figure it all out. It's not hard, I've just been really busy with working and haven't had the time with working with all the fun functions.
I also love that I don't have to take it off and protect it if I'm out hiking and get caught in a rain storm. I'm out almost every weekend walking in some nature trail or another. So I get caught in a few unexpected downpours while I'm out.
Now some of the more difficult "to do's" with the Misfit...
Setting the time isn't impossible, just need a lot of patience.
Using a magnifying glass, and good light, helped me get the misfit logo centered in that itty bitty hole at the 6 oclock mark. Whewww...
The watch doesn't have a backlight. So it's so hard to see the time in low light, impossible in the dark.
I wish it was thinner than it is. I'm not used to wearing a watch, or a fitness tracker, that is as thick as this one is.
I don't like the color of the watch band that came with the rose gold colored watch. All the other colored watches comes with a matching band. This watch comes with more silver colored band and silver buckle. Just doesn't look right. Might try to get that band replaced with something that looks better.
So far I am loving the Misfit. Love hearing that customer support is helpful in case I have a problem, like many has, with the crystal shattering.
text_fidelity_b: Misfit Phase Hybrid Wearables Smartwatch - Rose Gold

text_fidelity_a:
Zinwell ZAT-970A Digital to Analog TV Converter Box (for Antenna Use) We needed to save some money, and I'd heard that Over The Air broadcasts included channels you wouldn't otherwise get. My Dish TV account provided local channels and a whole bunch of channels I didn't use; but the OTA feature really helps!

I paired the Zinwell digital / analog converter box (highly rated, outstanding Amazon price) with the Radio Shack Antennacraft® HDX1000 Amplified HDTV Antenna (also highly rated). You should know one thing -- the mast size for the Dish TV is larger than the mast size for the Antennacraft antenna, so you can't just remove the Dish and replace it with the Antennacraft on the same mast. But it is an easy install.

As a trial, before going up to the roof (2 story house), I set the Antennacraft in the downstairs window that has a view to the southwest (the direction our local TV stations broadcast from). Without the Zinwell, you're limited to the low power analog stations (mostly Spanish language, a few home shopping stations). I think I got about 6 stations. Then I plugged in the Zinwell in line between the antenna and the TV (after disconnecting the Dish TV feed), did a scan, and had 20 channels. Repeated the process upstairs (remember, we have a 2 story) and had 22 channels!! All the local tv stations (NBC, ABC, CW, ION, PBS, etc.) that broadcast digitally came through great!! Unfortunately, it started raining :( so after the rain stopped, I only got as far as getting the mast installed outdoors before it got too dark. It won't take long to finish.

Only one Zinwell related item: You're supposed to be able to choose the feed from the Zinwell to the TV to be either Coax or the Composite (yellow video, red and white audio). I couldn't get the composite to work in setup, but the coax worked just fine. Haven't had a chance to see if, once programmed, the composite would work, or if for some reason I hooked it up to my tv incorrectly (hard to imagine), but ... since the coax works so well, and video and audio quality are great, I'm money ahead and not complaining!!

So when do I break even? $80 antenna plus 2 $40 boxes = $160; Dish TV was costing me about $55/month (yeah, once you've been a subscriber for a while, there's essentially no customer retention policy, so, good by Dish!! -- and that's probably true for Directv and Comcast, too). So after 3 months, essentially at the start of January, I'm home free!! Thanks, Amazon, you're helping me save money, and that's really great!!

NOTE: I only ordered one Zinwell to test out things, now I've ordered a second for our other TV (didn't want to put too much at risk if it didn't work, but it works great!).

NOTE 2: The gov't coupon program is long dead, no hope of getting $40 off on one, just be glad if you waited that these things are as reasonably priced as they are.
text_fidelity_b: Zinwell ZAT-970A Digital to Analog TV Converter Box (for Antenna Use)

Armor Suit MilitaryShield Screen Protector For Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 10.1 - [Max Coverage] Anti-Bubble HD Clear Film I bought this to keep the screen of my roughly $300 tablet safe from scratches. I watched the YouTube instruction video as the included instruction sheet asked. It took me two tries to put the screen on how I wanted it. By that time I had used almost all of the solution. I put the tablet on a dry, dust-free level surface and left it alone for over 24 hours, as instructed.

The screen protector doesn't quite fit the screen (and yes, I bought the correct shield for my tablet). There is a small portion on the left side of the screen that is not covered because the shield is all the way to the right edge of the screen. It has been three days and there are still bubbles under the shield, which makes me think I must have not pushed all the moisture out. The instructions said any imperfections such as micro-bubbles would go away on their own after a couple days. I guess I will see if they do.

The tablet still responds to touching with my fingertips with the shield on. I did notice that when I was using the tablet after installing the shield and waiting the specified time for it to dry that it was difficult to remove little bits and pieces of whatever debris from the environment falls on the screen. Wiping it away takes more effort because things seem to stick to the shield.

That said, I will say that the company seems to pride itself on service, which I appreciate. They include a quality microfiber cloth and a little plastic wedge (I don't know how else to describe it) to push bubbles and moisture from under the shield after it is applied, and the solution is in a quality thin, plastic spray bottle. They also really want feedback so it seems they are committed to improving their service. My rating is for the actual product, the installation required, and overall look, not the company itself.

Ring Video Doorbell (1st Gen) – 720p HD video, motion activated alerts, easy installation – Satin Nickel I'm an early adopter of lots of "smart everything" internet connected products (Nest stuff, Smart Grill, SmartVents, internet connected cars, etc.). I have found the Ring doorbell to be one of the most useful and reliable of these types of products. Remote functions that are really valuable to me:
* Remotely "greet" and reschedule the delivery guy who was 2 hours late, while you are out doing other other errands. Warning - it does really freak out most delivery guys to hear your voice emanating from the doorbell button !
* Receive confirmation that your tween/teen has made it home from school, even when they don't see fit to call or text. Plus do a body count to see if any "extras" are visiting. Plus also have a concrete, time-stamped log of any late night returns, so you don't have to stay up late to intercept returning teens.
* Capture video evidence of stolen packages, unwanted solicitations, and prowlers.
The cloud recording cost of 30$/yr is a far better value than other services like Next or Flir. Ring is the clear choice for door monitoring as well as a really cool doorbell.

My only caveats for buyers:
* Take care with the physical installation on very rough surfaces like rough stucco. Holes need to exactly align (no slotted mounting holes) plus the mount plate is sensitive to bending. If the most bends too much to conform to the wall, the actual button/bell unit will not attach.
* Make sure your WiFi signal is strong enough in the location where you are planning install the ring. Plaster and stucco (with embedded screening) attenuate WiFi signals. WiFi basestation with beam-forming really do help (one of my neighbors needed to swap an Apple Airport Express for an Airport Extreme Basestation to achieve reliable and no-laggy video, but now the Ring works like a charm)
* Make sure your transformer is putting out an in-spec voltage, for a wired installation. Mine worked fine, but the another neighbor who recommended the Ring to me wen through two units (replaced by Ring), before they determined the doorbell voltage from the transformer was too high. Things worked flawlessly with the third unit when my neighbor moved to unwired operation.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell (1st Gen) – 720p HD video, motion activated alerts, easy installation – Satin Nickel

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Tablet Mouse for Android 3.1+ You just cannot go wrong with a Logitech mouse, and this one is no exception. Sleek and sexy, well-designed and reliable, this tablet mouse for Android 3.1+ is a joy to hold. I love the color, too. It reminds me of my beloved old teal Logitech corded mouse that wouldn't work with the newer computers. This is a notebook-sized mouse, which is the size I prefer. It is not as tiny as some of the little mice out there, though. Not too big, not to small; just right.

Logitech stresses that this is an Android mouse and that it's not going to work properly with anything older than Android 3.1. It's even in the product title, so it's obvious that the OS is important, but I'm sure there will be people out there who will think it's going to work with earlier versions of Android. I wouldn't chance it. Some other reviewers have reported successfully pairing this mouse with non-Android systems, but I haven't been able to. It did happily meet and greet a friend's tablet PC, however.

Note that, unlike some Logitech mice, this mouse does NOT have a dongle, so you must have a bluetooth-enabled machine to use it. I tried it with a generic bluetooth dongle on my Windows Vista laptop, and I couldn't get it to work. That's not the mouse's fault. One good thing about it is that you can use it with a bluetooth keyboard; if I were going to get one, I'd go with Logitech's keyboard so I know they'll play nice.

I haven't had the opportunity to run down the batteries of this mouse, but if this one is like the other Logitech mice I own, the batteries last a long, long time--unlike competitors' mice, which seem to chew up and spit out batteries every few weeks. You can turn the mouse off, of course, but the sleep function also conserves batteries. Very nice.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Tablet Mouse for Android 3.1+

We had to use a binder to prop it up so the video would be high enough to watch comfortably. IF you do use a binder or another angled surface, at least one of the edges will be blurry so you'll have to adjust the keystone. Without the adjustment, think that one haikyuu scene where it zooms in on Aone's forehead as he goes to block the spike. The overall quality of the picture is fine, but the pixels could be finer because they're still kinda big. Also, the colors are not as vibrant, but they are still pretty good quality. While watching, the audio comes through the projector. IF you do use the audio through the projector, it is crunchy. I am talking crunchier than a freshly opened bag of frito's lays in a dead silent movie theater during a dramatic death scene. I would definitely suggest using an external speaker or audio output unless the projector's crunchy audio appeals to you and your loved ones.

tl;dr
could have more pixels
could have better color
definitely look into an alternative audio source
works well in small rooms
doesn't have to be super dark for the screen to show up (pretty bright)

text_fidelity_a:
(OLD MODEL) Seagate Expansion 3TB Desktop External Hard Drive USB 3.0 (STBV3000100) So far, the hard drive is working as one would expect. As always with these things, the questions mostly arise in longevity/reliability issues, so I'll be updating this once I've had a longer time to determine how it does in those categories. First impressions at this point, though:

1) the drive has a relatively small footprint, which is nice

2) Feels quite sturdy and hefty (it's surprisingly heavy) with good build quality

3) This isn't powered by your USB, so you'll need an outlet for its enclosed power cord

4) When you start up, it takes a little while (a few seconds) for the display light to come on. At first, I thought it hadn't started up at all, but just wait a small bit and it will light up

5) the display light is located on top but at the rear of the device, which while minor, is a slight inconvenience. I have it under my desk set back a little ways, so to see the light isn't as immediate as one might like

6) the drive is quite quiet. Not silent--you can hear it--but definitely quieter than many I've had

7) the drive is pretty fast, with the uptick from USB 2 to 3 very noticeable as I move from one computer (USB 2) to the other (USB 3)--it varies depending on what I'm copying, but sometimes the difference is half the speed

8) despite the small footprint, with its necessity for power and it's weight, I wouldn't consider this at all a portable drive, though I suppose you could use it as such. But really, it's big and heavy for that.

9) I use this on several Macs--no problem at all reformatting it for those computers--just a few mouse clicks and a few seconds is all

So far, this is a good big backup drive (I have the 5 TB version). And since we all know, or should, that drives will fail, you can't have too many of them. If any issues arise over time, I'll update accordingly
text_fidelity_b: (OLD MODEL) Seagate Expansion 3TB Desktop External Hard Drive USB 3.0 (STBV3000100)

This enclosure is heavy, and not bad looking. The plastic faceplate comes off easy (as it was probably designed to do, to allow easy changing the Hard Drives). But again chances are once you get the drives installed and settings just so, you will not be messing with the door/faceplate. it has tow plastic pins on the bottom and a "latch (Spring loaded)" press and it pops off or on.
The power cord goes in the side, which is weird but not a deal breaker. And unusual configuration, but it is pretty solid and really I don't really mess with it very oftern).
Three fan settings and yes two of them are not quiet. I leave mine on auto and unless I am working on a hot day, moving or writing tons of files, don't hear the fan at all).
The LED lights are not an issue for me, but I could see where in a dark room it would bother some folks. (electrical tape if it really errkks you).
Getting the settings the way you want them takes some trial and error, but once you have them you will most likely not mess with them again.
Drives are easy to add or remove, a couple screws, slide it in the slot.
I have found that if the drive has been formatted and contains data when you add it, you have to force mount it, but once that is done no issues.
So if possible initialize the drive in the enclosure.
This is ideal for novice of mid-level tech geeks, or folks who have a large media collection (Music, movies, photos, etc).
I have hooked it up directly to my Mac Pro and my Wireless router (Orbi) so anyone authorized to access the network can access the media files on it. So my Photos on one drive, Movies on two drives and music on the last drive.
I would highly recommend this to anyone wanting to create a media server.
It DOES NOT have RAID built-in, it can be added via software, but, for a few bucks more you can get the RAID version of this.

text_fidelity_a:
Echo (3rd Gen)- Smart speaker with Alexa- Charcoal I'm not paranoid (famous last words). No, really, I welcome my personal assistant overlords. My family is pretty vanilla. So it only creeps me out a little when my husband and I have "test" discussions about things we don't talk about, don't search the internet for, and would never actually buy in a million years only to see such items pushed to us in advertising feeds. Is one of our assistants listening when it is supposed to be asleep? If so, which one? All three of the majors are in our house. Both of the cats have turned Siri on by walking across my laptop. And Alexa hears her name sometimes inexplicably. Maybe it's my husband's Long Island accent?

Or maybe it is just randomness and the assistants are functioning as advertised. Either way, I won't be getting rid of them anytime soon. The Echo Plus recognized all but two of my smart bulbs and found all of my switches and everything else that still works (old WeMo stuff went offline over a year ago when Belkin pushed a firmware upgrade and killed their wifi connections). It has controlled them flawlessly so far, and this has allowed me to free up the ethernet ports I'd dedicated to several different hubs.

My Echo devices are the ones we use most around here, both because the house runs on Amazon Prime and Subscribe and Save (I have lupus and cannot easily shop in the real world) AND because the Echos allow me to reach my teenager and tell him things whether he wants to hear them or not. He can ignore my texts and refuse to answer the phone, but Alexa lets me yell at him from anywhere in the world. (And the app lets me see his history of ridiculous teenaged boy questions - unlike Siri, Alexa is not a potty mouth and does not like it when you are.)

On the downside, Alexa won't give you suggestions if she doesn't know something. She just gives you an Elizabeth Jennings (The Americans) type, "Hmmm," and a disappointed note.

The Echo Plus also seems to "hear" better and have fewer false activations. And the sound is better for music - by a surprising amount. So, if Alexa has a place in your home, the Echo Plus is a good way to get her. Four stars. I'd give five if the wake word were more customizable.
text_fidelity_b: Echo (3rd Gen)- Smart speaker with Alexa- Charcoal

GE Personal Security Keychain Alarm, Extra Loud 120 Decibel Siren, Pull Pin Activated, Built In LED Light, Personal & Portable Safety, Emergency, Self Defense, Easy to Use, 51208 I bought several of these for our home and my mother's home. Super loud, and will stop or at least make it difficult for a door to be opened wide enough for an intruder to enter. I tested one out on my husband by placing it at the door he normally enters through. It stopped him, scared him and did just what I hoped it would do. He kind of got mad at me and hollered a few explicatives but it was worth it! We have one door that is on a raised threshold so I set the door stop alarm on a book and the door hits it squarely when opened just a little bitty bit. It's loud - ear piercing loud and that's good as it should scare the bejeebers out of a bad person. On doors that have windows through which the unwanted guest might peer through and see the doorstop, just by placing a light weight towel or papers over it disguises completely. They'll just think your a slob and leave newspapers on the floor.

My mom was thrilled with her doorstops. Anything to help parents stay safe is money well-spent.

Be aware of how all of your doors open since they won't do any good on doors that open to the outside. The 9 volt battery was a tad difficult to install but I'm not complaining. For my mom I had to write in big letters with a felt permanent marker ON and OFF so she could easily turn them off when not in use and not waste batteries or scare her by an accidental alarm. We'll be taking some of these with us on vacation. These are really great!

UPDATE: December 1, 2011 - I have bought several more of these because they are so practical and good at what they do. I've learned to pick them up by holding the sides of them lest I accidentally hit the metal plate on top and hear it's ear-breaking scream. I've taken at least one of these on overnight trips to put against the door in our hotel rooms. It makes me feel a lot safer knowing this thing will scream if someone tries to break in.
text_fidelity_b: GE Personal Security Keychain Alarm, Extra Loud 120 Decibel Siren, Pull Pin Activated, Built In LED Light, Personal & Portable Safety, Emergency, Self Defense, Easy to Use, 51208

I then have to crop the image and make it bigger for it to show. The auto-scan option didn't work at all. text_fidelity_a:
Canon Office Products MG5420 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier I've had problems with Pixmas in the past, mostly having to do with wireless networks and having to reinstall the software over and over to try to get them to hang on to network settings. I can't guarantee that this printer is going to be any better in the long run, but the set-up actually works pretty well if you use the standard version, not the WPS... and I'm getting way ahead of myself on this one.

To begin with, the printer requires a lot of time for set-up. You're not going to be doing this on the fly, so set aside an hour or so to: 1) remove all the tape of which there is much, 2) read over the instructions 3) install the ink, 4) run a print alignment 5) set up your wireless connection (about which more in a moment) 6) install the software (which takes a good 15 minutes or more), and 7) put the machine (and yourself) through its paces. Yeah, it's going to take a while.

Now I know you can read about the features on your own, so I'm here to tell you about the things that work for me and those that don't. First off, the wireless set-up is confusing. Choose Standard instead of WPS and save yourself some headaches unless you're a computer whiz kid. After the third error message in the WPS set-up I went to standard, entered my pass code and had the connection up and running in about a minute.

Once that was done and the software was installed I fired up the Canon Image Garden. First I scanned an image and attempted to rotate, crop and fix any deficiencies I found. The scan was over sharp and looked a bit jagged, but a little fiddling with the Canon software fixed that. Canon software also rotated and cropped perfectly. One really nice feature is that they remind you to put the printing side of the paper down in the paper cassette. How many pieces of paper will that save?

The biggest complaint I had was that it didn't give me a choice of which paper cassette to use for printing, so I got a ridiculously truncated image on the first try. I believe it chooses the paper based on the size of the image, which I get, but at the same time that limits flexibility in printing. I opened another photo processing program and it allowed me to print from whatever cassette I liked. Coupled with a better suite of applications for correction and enhancement, I think it's safe to say that I'll be using the Canon software almost never.

Printing on plain paper is clearly not going to be as satisfactory as it is on glossy, but in some cases I found it surprisingly good, good enough to give you an idea of what sort of image you're going to end up with when you switch to photo paper. It's also more than good enough for printing out emails and web pages.

Scanning and printing are both pretty fast, another plus. And the copy function works pretty seamlessly without any sort of computer interface. Just punch a couple of buttons and Bob's your uncle! It does take a bit of time to warm up and is a little noisy but no more so than any Canon printer I've ever used. It's not bothersome, in my opinion. You might feel otherwise.

Inks are easy to install, but you'll find refills pricey, no question. I suspect off-brand ones are available or will be soon enough.

In short, it's a good, inexpensive printer for a home or home office. Use photo paper and settings and get the full quality the MG5420 is capable of producing; I think it's pretty remarkable. The photos I printed out are as good as or in one case, better than the original. That's a powerful recommendation in my book.
text_fidelity_b: Canon Office Products MG5420 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon 55-200mm f/4-5.6G ED IF AF-S DX VR [Vibration Reduction] Nikkor Zoom Lens Bulk packaging (White box, New) An upgrade of Nikon's original digital-only tele kit zoom, this new 55-200mm f/4-5.6 ($250, street) adds Vibration Reduction and a number of optical improvements for only $70 more. A 3.6X 82-300mm equivalent zoom, it's not expected to be bundled in Nikon DSLR kits any time soon.

Hands on:

The barrel, when contracted, is nearly an inch longer than the earlier 55-200mm non-VR DX lens, but is still extremely light as a result of all-plastic construction, including the lensmount. The large zoom ring's slightly uneven and underdamped turning action is what you'd expect from a lens at this price. The narrow manual-focusing ring is even-turning but also underdamped, with a very short turning radius for fast, if coarse, manual focusing. AF action on our test camera, the D40x, was adequately fast and quiet, thanks to Nikon's Silent Wave Motor in the lens.

In the lab:

SQF tests found Excellent sharpness and contrast at all focal lengths -- an improvement over the earlier, non-VR version of this lens. DxO Analyzer 2.0 tests found Imperceptible barrel distortion at 55mm (0.08%), and Slight pincushion distortion at 105mm and 200mm (0.24% and 0.19%, respectively). All three are also improvements over the earlier lens. Light falloff was gone from the corners by f/5 at 55mm, f/7.1 at 105mm, and f/8 at 200mm.

At the uniform close-focusing distance of approximately 43.5 inches, tests of close-up ability found maximum magnification ratios ranging from 1:14.25 at 55mm to 1:3.8 at 200mm, about an average magnifying power, and not up to the 1:3.4 turned in by the non-VR 55-200mm. DxO Analyzer Blur tests of the lens' first-generation VR system (at 200mm) showed an improvement for three users of about 3 stops of extra handheld sharpness at slower shutter speeds; 4 stops are possible with Nikon's VR II system.

Conclusions:

Even though it's the earlier version of VR, to get any VR at this price is a steal.
text_fidelity_b: Nikon 55-200mm f/4-5.6G ED IF AF-S DX VR [Vibration Reduction] Nikkor Zoom Lens Bulk packaging (White box, New)

ESSLNB Astronomy Binoculars 13-39X70 Zoom Giant Binoculars with Tripod Adapter Phone Adapter and Case Binoculars for Bird Watching Hunting and Stargazing (13-39X70) First thing that you need to know about this particular pair of binoculars is the sheer size means this is not your usual "pack around" set of optics. Having expected that from the description of this item, I had some fairly specific plans for it. Living in rural Eastern Oregon, we do a lot of wildlife viewing and stargazing. The night skies here are incredible since there is almost no light pollution to deal with and the wide open range here offers a lot of very long range wildlife viewing. For these purposes, this pair of binoculars works splendidly. They are easier to manipulate and set up than our telescopes for spur of the moment viewing sessions.

Being as large as they are, and very heavy, a good quality sturdy tripod is an absolute must, especially at the higher magnification. My sons and I have had no trouble at all setting the focus for our individual needs. The optics are pretty bright, thanks to the 80mm objective lens diameter. The large front lens also offers you a much wider field of view, which is great when you are trying to find your target. Speaking of target, we also use these as a secondary spotting scope when doing recreational shooting. While not on par with optics such as Zeiss or Swarovski, you are paying only a fraction of that price. In this price range, I feel that these binoculars give you fantastic bang for the buck.

These come with a very durable rubberized coating, so should stand up to average bumps and bruises. This also helps with your grip. I have used this in subfreezing temperatures and in the rain with no signs of influence from the elements.

I have yet to utilize this particular phone adapter yet, so I can't really speak to its effectiveness. It does, however seem very similar to other adapters I have received for various other optics.
text_fidelity_b: ESSLNB Astronomy Binoculars 13-39X70 Zoom Giant Binoculars with Tripod Adapter Phone Adapter and Case Binoculars for Bird Watching Hunting and Stargazing (13-39X70)

At 3000:1 the contrast is very nice and better than most at this price range, and essentially all TN/IPS.

This is why I like VA panels, the black levels and the contrast. I've always bought IPS before and they're still great obviously, but after having a VA television, I started to personally prefer its benefits. There are obviously a few downsides when it comes to VA monitors, but this particular model solves most of them.

I have 2 IPS displays on both sides of this, and I can tell you the colors look excellent. It was also close to perfect calibration right out of the box, which was a nice change.

One review mentioned Gamma Mode 1 as closer to 2.2, but another comment mentioned Gamma Mode 3. Mode 3 seemed closest to me when calibrating, so I would recommend it.

Viewing angles:

The viewing angles aren't very good, as expected, but it doesn't affect me as I'm always right in front of my monitors. There is some slight vignetting when sitting close, so a curved screen could have been nice if implemented well.

Backlight bleed:

Having no IPS glow or backlight bleed is another benefit. With larger VA tvs there can occasionally be some slight blobbiness when in very dark settings, but this panel is very uniform with no BLB that I can see.

Size/pixel density:

I personally love bigger monitors, and don't have an issue with the pixel density here. Some people who are more sensitive to that might not be completely satisfied, but I personally would choose the increased immersion of a larger panel. Regardless, 1440p is awesome.

Ghosting/input lag:

In terms of ghosting, it's surprisingly almost nonexistent. Here's some comments from other people:

"I played some Doom last night, and literally did nothing but rapidly move my camera all over the place to see if I could notice any ghosting or bleeding. I couldn't find anything objectionable..."

"Also there is very little ghosting in the monitor which is super rare for VA panels."

"...even in dark games like Outlast 2/Doom, the ghosting is so hard to see that you have to intentionally find a worst case scenario to try and induce it."

"Ghosting is slight, about on par with 165 Hz IPS gaming panels from my testing. Only TN is faster really."

In terms of input lag, tftcentral says: "We measured a total display lag of only 6.40ms. With approximately 4.15ms of that accounted for by pixel response times we had an estimated signal processing of just 2.25ms, which was next to nothing. This is in keeping with other G-sync screens we have tested, as the absence of an additional scaler (and presence of the G-sync module) allows for extremely low lag."

This monitor is exactly what I've been waiting for. The circular light bar on the back is a nice touch as well, although it could be a bit brighter. I also would have preferred a sharpness slider, but it's not entirely necessary.

FYI, it can be freely moved in basically every direction, including 90 degree rotation - if you need that for some reason.

So if you don't have issues with viewing angles/slightly higher pixel density, this is an excellent choice as it excels in basically every other area.
text_fidelity_b: LG 32GK850G-B 32" QHD Gaming Monitor with 144Hz Refresh Rate and NVIDIA G-Sync,Black

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire HD 8.9", 8.9" HD display, 16 GB or 32 GB, Wi-Fi or Optional 4G LTE Wireless (Previous Generation - 2nd) As with the original Fire, the out of box experience is very nicely done. Very straightforward process of just turning it on and letting the tablet register and update itself. It took about 10 minutes (with the majority of the time waiting for an update to download) and it was ready to go. It picked up all my original Fire music and books from the cloud and most of my Fire apps. I was disappointed to see that a couple of my favorite apps (TED Talks and Play Music Videos Free) were judged not compatible with my new Fire. Hopefully updates will be coming soon.

The screen is delightful! Crisp and clear, and a marked increase in resolution versus the original Fire. Videos on the HD Fire are simply amazing.

The sound quality is also a marked improvement. While it was pretty much mandatory to hook up an external speaker for the original Fire, the new Fire puts out pretty decent sound quality all on its own. I still hook it up to external speakers (I'm partial to the Bose Companion 20) for movies and music when I'm at my desk, but it puts out more than adequate sound all on its own.

Response time is more snappy than the original Fire, and the carousel is easier to navigate (smoother scrolling). Picking up a WiFi signal seems to be better with the new fire - I'm getting all signal strength bars displayed in areas of the house where I could only get 2 or 3 bars with the original Fire.

The form factor is great for video watching. The extra screen size makes a big difference. The other huge advantage to the size is typing. It's MUCH easier to see and use the onscreen keyboard than on the original Fire. I had no problems typing without a stylus; on the original Fire a stylus is a must.

So far I don't see many misses other than a hard-to-find power button. The casing and build quality is not at the same level as an iPad, but neither is the price. I'm very pleased with the price-performance level of the HD Fire.

This is not replacing my original Fire - I'll continue to use that for most of my book reading and when I need portability. For everything else, the larger screen is well worth the additional cost.

I have a Nexus 7, the iPad 2 and an HP Touchpad and the Fire is my favorite by far. Not because either the original or this new Fire are the best in terms of build quality or speed or tech specs, but for one simple reason: the Fire makes it so incredibly easy to avail myself of entertainment and content. The tight link to the Amazon ecosystem is, for me, a huge plus - it keeps my entertainment pipeline full of things I want to read, listen to or watch with little or no effort on my part. And, best of all, a lot of that content is free through Prime.

Love it, and highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire HD 8.9", 8.9" HD display, 16 GB or 32 GB, Wi-Fi or Optional 4G LTE Wireless (Previous Generation - 2nd)

Ring Chime Pro I'm an early adopter. Ring isn't perfect, but it's the most consistent security brand for mostly getting it right or almost right mostly 90% of the time. Compared to the MANY others I've bought, used for a few months, and abandoned, this is high praise.

But setting up a 2.4ghz device is hard these days. Phones don't tell you whether you're on 2.4ghz or 5 anymore. I keep an old iPad around JUST to set up smart things.

-aside- you know what would be smart? a smart thing that only feeds the 2.4 part of your network to you as a connection choice. Instead of which of these 4 networks only one of which is 2.4 should I connect to, a real smart device doesn't offer 5gHz networks as a choice.

Or, you know, just modernize the wifi cards.

Anyway. This didn't even do that. It connected to the other chime pro (older much) and then asked to connect to the wifi network. It updated itself in under a minute, and done. And now my back cams aren't dropping offline.

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black) I made absolutely sure everything was closed before putting it into water, not that one could have much faith in the mechanisms keeping it closed, as they are easy to accidentally open. I put it in the water gently, and only a foot or so, to film some stingrays and fish; this recording went fine. Later that day, I wanted to photograph a tiny little crab. I took one picture from above the water, and one from below. I noticed this time, when I put the camera underwater, that bubbles started to come out the top. I immediately took it out and noticed the screen starting to fog up with condensation and moisture, the first very bad sign. I double checked everything was still closed, and it was. No part of it had been opened. I put it back in, hoping for the best. After coming back to the sand (never having done more than a few feet underwater), I tried to turn it on to get some video. It would not turn on. I checked again, and nothing appeared to be open. I then dried the exterior and opened it, only to discover there was water on the inside. I immediately removed the SD card, in hopes of salvaging it, but the camera was (is) completely dead.

Two days later, there is corrosion forming on the inside from the water, but at least I salvaged the content on the SD card. The results? Video quality is fine above and below water. Photo quality is a mess. Absolutely the worst pics imaginable.
I am so glad I didn't have to pay for this product; I would have been furious it didn't even last a day in the ocean.

I expected more, since I had previously purchased a "Kodak EasyShare Sport C123 12 MP Waterproof Digital Camera", which has been great! That product never failed after much abuse and takes decent picture and video. I'm not sure what happened here, but buyer beware! Try the EasyShare Sport instead.

I'll post some pictures and, if it lets me, some video too. I hope you all find this helpful!

UPDATE: I can't post video (sorry)
Also, I looked at some other reviews that mentioned water getting in while at the pool or in other non-salinated water. Bear in mind that many electronics can survive water immersion if it is fresh water (as opposed to salt water). Many of these reviewers gave the camera more than one star because it was able to work again, but bear in mind this will NOT hold true it Salt water enters the device. Please consider this.
text_fidelity_b: Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
PixelFlash No-Bend Pins USB 3 CF Card Reader, Compact Flash Card Reader, Tactical SuperSpeed CompactFlash Memory Adapter, Rugged Anti-Scratch Exterior Classic Card Reader - White I was delighted to try out this CompactFlash reader, because my Canon camera uses CF cards, and my laptop has no card reader. My new computer will be lacking a CompactFlash card reader as well.

The claim of having pins that don't bend sounds extremely attractive to me, since I've tossed out a card reader in the past for getting bent pins that were hard to straighten.

While I didn't get to test out the USB 3.0 function of this card reader, it worked great on my regular USB 2.0 connections and speedily transferred over 500 photos in just a couple of minutes.

The only criticism I have of this card reader is that the profile is thick enough that on my computer, where I have two USB ports stacked one on top of another, I need to unplug something in order to be able to plug in this card reader. This isn't a big deal, since I have little USB extension cords that I can use if I truly don't want to unplug something else, but if the manufacturers are listening, I'd love to see a slimmer profile on any future models.

Overall, this is a fast, reasonably priced, handy little card reader that I'm glad to add to my collection of tech toys.

text_fidelity_a:
PANASONIC Wings Sport Headphones are Ultra-Light Wireless Bluetooth Sport Earbud 3D Flex Sport Clips with Microphone and Call/Volume Controller, IPX5 Rated Water-Resistant - RP-BTS35-K (Black) I received these earphones from Amazon Vine in early January, 2018. I liked the over-the-ears design. It makes the earphones far less likely to fall off when exercising. The sound quality is also excellent. I found its wireless bluetooth function quite handy for listening to music on my smartphone while walking, biking, lifting weights or doing calisthenics.

In short, as long as the battery could be charged, these sport earphones worked quite well. But suddenly, a few weeks ago, after only 7 months of use, the battery simply would no longer take a charge. The manual says that the battery should last through up to 300 charges, and there is absolutely no way that in only seven months I charged this device 300 times. It holds a charge well while the battery is working, much better than the other bluetooth earbuds that I have owned. So I could use it for up to five days without charging the battery. This means that, in seven months, I only charged the battery about 42-50 times, at most. This means the life of the battery was a mere 16% of what the manufacturer promised!

This is not a device in which the battery can be replaced. Therefore, once the battery dies, the earphones are worthless. Since the warranty is only for 90 days, there is no recourse with the manufacturer for replacing this device after that length of time.

The way that this product works is a good idea, but until the design includes the possibility of replacing the battery, the high price is simply not worth it. I will have to stick to cheap earbuds which are not such a hit to my pocketbook when their non-replaceable battery dies.

I rate this product as follows:

Sound quality 5 stars
Durability of battery: 1 star
Value for price: 1 star
Overall average: 2.3 stars
text_fidelity_b: PANASONIC Wings Sport Headphones are Ultra-Light Wireless Bluetooth Sport Earbud 3D Flex Sport Clips with Microphone and Call/Volume Controller, IPX5 Rated Water-Resistant - RP-BTS35-K (Black)

I've purchased a few of these. One did fail after a few years of intense use (I play Diablo 3 and a few MMOs, along with regular productivity/internet surfing.) Considering the price, and the amount of use these get, I have nothing but praise for these devices.

I will be honest: I reluctantly purchased this device. I've been using trackballs since around 1997 because my original computer space didn't really accommodate a standard mouse, and I really haven't gone back to mice. The corded Logitech Trackman has been my favored trackball for years. My cat chewed through the cord, and it eventually stopped working right, so I had to upgrade. Having a wireless trackball has always seemed rather redundant to me; why would you need cordless when you never move it? Well, it's actually quite nice to not fiddle with the cord! I didn't realize how annoying having a tether is until you no longer have it...

At any rate, this trackball is remarkably accurate (I play several games and work with large spread sheets,) and a snap to install. In short, a reluctant customer is very satisfied!

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG Galaxy Buds Live True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds w/ Active Noise Cancelling, Charging Case, AKG Tuned 12mm Speaker, Long Battery Life, US Version, Mystic Red I bought mine direct from Samsung and ultimately returned them. I found that I had to fiddle with them constantly to hit the sweet spot for the music to sound like it should instead of like I was listening through a tin can, and while fiddling with them the touch controls become an annoying hassle because you are trying to get the fit right and the music is turning on and off and pausing and skipping, etc, because you are touching them. The buds can't seem to differentiate at all between an actual hold/grip to manipulate them in your ears, and a tap as you would do to actually use a touch control feature.

Don't quote me on this because it's not like I counted every review that appeared male vs female, but I found that they hurt and I think it might be because they were designed by somewhat larger-eared males. I originally assumed the hurty issue was likely because they were designed by some 60 year old man engineer with huge ears (because ears grow our whole lives) and so they were only made to fit kind of older larger ears. I even wrote on my Samsung review that they should have made the fit for the age group of their customer. But now, reading these Amazon reviews, I am noticing that the people saying they fit great seem to mostly be male names and those saying they hurt seem to mostly be female-normative names, so I still think they were designed for larger ears, but maybe for males they will fit better - I truly don't know how different in size male vs female ears are though; it's just a random observation of these reviews of hurt vs feel great.

Bottom line, they hurt my ears and were too picky about being perfectly aligned in my ear. On the rare occasion I hit that sweet spot they sounded great and never felt like they were going to fall out. Too bad it took so much effort to find that spot.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG Galaxy Buds Live True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds w/ Active Noise Cancelling, Charging Case, AKG Tuned 12mm Speaker, Long Battery Life, US Version, Mystic Red

The magnetic connection is reasonably strong, though the magnets could be stronger. The other bit, the part that plug into the charging cord, doesn’t always “click” on the first attempt.

text_fidelity_a:
Apple 2020 iPad Air (10.9-inch, Wi-Fi + Cellular, 64GB) - Green (4th Generation) Or, at least, a laptop go away until I can afford a better laptop-er.

So far, this is not that. For one thing, the expensive keyboard case has amazing keys, but in a tiny little format that isn't really easy to type on quickly, if you are used to using all of both of your hands. The action is way better than my laptop's, but it's cramped.

Having a trackpad is lovely. It was what I had been waiting for before upgrading from my gen1 iPad Air. But the case again interferes with functionality because you can't really adjust the iPad angle. The iPad itself is sleek and gorgeous. And it's a lot faster than my old iPad. And it has a lot more space in it. And - in theory - it should run app versions of everything I use my laptop for.

In theory.

And it almost does.

Kind of.

But it's a pain and a half to set up. Its security features won't let it transfer passwords from my other devices, which means that all of those passwords I let Apple suggest for me (before I learned the hard way that Apple doesn't always save them after setting them) - I have to enter by hand on the iPad. Mind you, I got the iPad's settings from a backup of a different iPad that had all those passwords already. Anyway, I can't even think of getting rid of my laptop, because I need it to look up my passwords so that I can enter them on the iPad.

(Yes, I know it's supposed to be as easy at turning on the keychain. It's not, though.)

Bottom lines? Yes, it's pretty and fast. No, it's not worth the money, and I wouldn't buy it again (I would either get a mini to do phone games and quick emails or shell out for the big iPad Pro and be done with laptops forever once I got my passwords in that one). Yes, I'm keeping it and am open to changing my mind.
text_fidelity_b: Apple 2020 iPad Air (10.9-inch, Wi-Fi + Cellular, 64GB) - Green (4th Generation)

-There is a lot of control available for turning up and down different sounds in shows and movies

-The wireless subwoofer is a big plus. The less cords the better, we have it about 5 feet from the sound bar and the connection between the two is reliable.

Cons:

After actually using through a morning commute, I'm confident with the conclusion that these are either knock-offs or refurbished. They have horrible sound output!

I'm not am audiophile and I don't expect stock earbuds to "wow" me with their amazing range. But with these there's NO bass whatsoever. The range seems to be limited to the higher notes. I guess another was of putting it is that these are a GREAT pair of $7.00 earbuds. They don't seem like a decent replacement for the stock Samsung earbuds that came with my Note 4.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity - Includes Special Offers For years, I used the keyboard kindle after it first came out and loved the "classic" look of the page so much. After replacing it several times due to screen issues, I finally made the switch to the paperwhite with some skepticism, thinking the back-light would make it into yet another screen I look at. I was pleasantly surprised that even the brighter settings still look like a page, and I can turn it all the way down for the same effect as my older model kindle. Plus, I don't need to bother anyone with a light anymore when I read in bed, in the car at night, etc.

Paying a bit extra for no ads was worth it, and I enjoy the drawings that serve as screensavers. The home page is not my favorite - I would prefer to default to my library list instead of wading through recommendations, etc. - but it's not that much of a hassle to tap over to the library screen. When I'm reading a book, it automatically opens to the page I left off on just like my old kindle.

I only vaguely miss having the 3G function my old kindle had because I used to live out in the boonies with limited internet access. However, the WiFi has been generally sufficient and now I just make sure I download a few books before I travel.

Overall, the kindle has definitely revolutionized the way I read since it first came out when I was in high school. I do still keep a lot of hard copies of my favorite series and enjoy reading real books from time to time, but the kindle is SO easy to download anything, anytime you want. Not to mention bringing a whole library with you in one slim package while traveling! I have had this model for a year and a half now, and have no issues or complaints at this time.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity - Includes Special Offers

I even connected it to my father's printer and he is concerned that he won't know what to do when I move out so I suggested he buy a Chromebook because they are priced very well and SO easy to use! He and my mother could not understand their Windows machine which was SO SLOW... I tried restoring it so many times and it just wasn't worth using. I just used my android phone for everything until I got this! Oh - and I love the heftiness .. my last one was so thin and light that I didn't really like that... this one has weight on it, just a bit and I like that. :-) Okay - enough gloating for me, just go buy one!!!! :-D

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th) I'm not going to delve into the technical aspects of the Fire as others have done an admirable job already. But as an alternative to other, more expensive tablets, the Fire is an amazing piece of tech.

I was almost getting ready to pull the trigger on the Google Pixel C or Samsung S3. A big leap for me as I didn't want to spend $500 plus on a tablet, but I wanted fast speed, large screen, and inexpensive aftermarket accessories.

The Fire is dual-core, so it flies through the games I play. A big plus. I know everyone hates when their game bogs down in the middle of a rousing Orc battle, or, even worse, won't even load. The Fire has run all the games I've thrown at it with no issues.

The 10" screen is heavenly, considering I came from a generic 7" tablet that was VGA on a good day. The text is crisp, the graphics flow as they should. HD movies and shows are freakin' excellent. The 10" format seems to be the best for this.

If you research well for accessories, you can find some nice deals. There was no way I was going to spring for a $30 case, when the $10 Fintie case works as good or better. More money saved for movies, games, and books!

Please don't spend the extra $15 on the 'without special offers' option. The only special offers thrown at you are when the tablet wakes from sleep. A quick swipe and they're gone. Save that money for a case!

And yes, Virginia, you can get the google play store. The easiest way is to install 4 app files and run them in order. No rooting, no PC hookups. Go to blog.ebook-reader dot com and search 'how to install google play on fire.' Easy peasy, just follow the instructions to the letter.

All-in-all this a capable tablet offered by Amazon. The price is right, the tech is excellent considering its price point. You can game like a madman, watch shows, and read War & Peace.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th)

text_fidelity_a:
Sena 20S-01D Motorcycle Bluetooth 4.1 Communication System with HD Audio and Advanced Noise Control (Dual) This thing is loaded with features,
It will take me awhile to remember all the functions (push this 1,2, or 3 times, or in combo), but typically you only use a personal few, so it gets better.
I have smartphone Bluetooth cell as both phone and music source - and that works well, though the sound for music isn't awesome (though I haven't others to compare to, I just know what great sounds like at the gym, and these sound tinny or music) - but I bought these as communicators first and music second.
You need to read the instructions over and over again, and the handy cards need to be kept with you on the bike ( there is no way you'll remember everything this thing can do).
The ambient mic feature is an interesting bonus.... Not only do they use that to adjust volume and sensitivity , you can activate it to hear into earphones which is handy when I pull up to customs or drive thought and need to hear what's being said.
FM radio works awesome.
The mic that comestibles your mouth allows you to start talking to your babe or bud and fades the music right away, but it isn't perfect as the music doesn't fade back in as well as I'd want (it thinks ambient noise after you both stop talking might still be voices so it kinda cuts in as chunks), so I prefer to just hit the button to initiate discussions and then hit it again when we're done (though that an be annoying too if there's a string of short discussions).
The other thing is it is supposed to allow you to give voice commands for most key tasks while riding (instead of reaching and finding buttons)... So your driving along and listening to tunes (or not), and say "hello Sena"... That activates the command prompts to speed dial somebody, turn on/off music or radio, or go to next song, or lots of stuff.... It works great in your living room but rarely ever while riding, and I've played with all the levels or think I have. I wish you could use whistling into the mic as a triggering option.... Good news is you quickly learn where the button is for forcing voice prompting so you don't have to keep talking to yourself forever...
There's also this double tap feature that is supposed kick in voice prompting when you tap the unit twice... Great idea, but despite many taps, many places, and not just softly, I only managed to get that to kick once in a month of efforts of the bike.
And yes practice all this in your living room because you don't want to be distracted on the bike. I did the livingroom thing and still took a lot of short rides to realize there's a lot to learn.
Despite what may seem like gloom above, this is one powerful, feature packed unit which has a lot of things I wanted, but I need to get better at, or for firmware updates to continually improve (which they have been).

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak PlaySport (Zx3) HD Waterproof Pocket Video Camera (Purple) There's a lot to like about the Playsport. For one, it's very easy to use as a point and shoot should be. The picture quality is certainly fine for just about anybody's use, save for those who really like blowing their pictures up large. It's very fast to move between photos and movie--a few thumb moves is all it takes. The same for toggling between the movie quality. Which means if you suddenly want to grab a still photo while videoing or are worried about recording room and want to drop down a notch or two in quality, you can do so without missing a lot of action. The zoom is a 3X, which is serviceable. I'd prefer longer and I'm sure the next version will offer a longer zoom, but as I use this for quick shots of the family and not for event shooting, the 3X is rarely an issue in terms of not being adequate.

Transfer of files is easy and fast (I use a Mac) and all the cables come bundled with it. Yes, you read that right--it ships with all the needed cables.

Because it is so small and slim, and held in that vertical position, it can get a bit shaky and you'll need to pay attention to keeping it steady, more so than larger cameras or ones you hold with two hands horizontally. The sound pickup is fine save that wind noise can be a problem on windy days--it'll wash out a good deal of the speaking sound.

It feels rugged out of the box and the number of times I've dropped it, including just recently while chasing my boy and his friend around the corner of the house and getting my foot caught in the extension cord of the Halloween decorations. I watched the camera skid across several feet of concrete sidewalk but it was none the worse for wear.

It's slimness makes it a great pocket camera--one of those where it's defined as such not because you can cram it into your pocket and walk around like you have a grapefruit in there but where it slips right in and you barely notice it. That's one of the reasons it's become the camera I take most often when I know I won't need a larger zoom or a flash.

I haven't tried the underwater aspect in actual underwater conditions (snorkeling, say), but a few practice photos in the pool shows it takes pretty sharp photos in that environment. But I'll leave the gauging of that aspect to those more well-versed in such a need.

In the end, it's a great little camera and as mentioned, it's quickly become the one I carry along most often when we're just heading out for some family fun. For post-dusk indoor, I take a Canon elph and for events or hiking a Canon IS with a 12x zoom and a tele-converter. But for playing games in the yard, birthday parties, classroom events, etc.--the Kodak has become the go-to camera.

highly recommended
text_fidelity_b: Kodak PlaySport (Zx3) HD Waterproof Pocket Video Camera (Purple)

text_fidelity_a:
(Discontinued) HP ENVY 32-Inch Screen LED-Lit Monitor Quad-HD There's a lot to like about this monitor, but also some clear drawbacks. Let's start with the good news.

In typical HP fashion it comes very well packaged to survive pretty much any measure of rough handling in transit. There's a "quick start" guide that is taped to the front of the monitor that walks you through the setup (which is very straightforward). There's also an excellent user guide in PDF on the included disk.

The overall design is very attractive. It's very slim, lightweight and easy to position. I'm using it with the included table stand since my wall-mount options can't handle a monitor this large (it does come with a metal plate with VESA-compatible holes should you want to use it with a mount).

I used this on both a PC and as a video monitor hooked up through my AV receiver. For both situations I used the HDMI interface.

The sound quality is very good compared with the typical built-in speaker. It lacks bass "punch" but is quite acceptable.

Now for the so-so news: picture quality. It's good, but not "wow" good. Picture quality was somewhat drab looking, lacking crispness and contrast despite spending a lot of time tweaking the video quality with the many options available. It becomes worse when viewed off center (although it does have a decent viewing angle).

It comes with a remote which could be very handy for switching inputs, tweaking the picture, adjusting the sound, etc. I say it "could be" since the remote it comes with is horrible. It's small, which is good, but all the buttons are flush mount and have black on black lettering. It is very, very hard to see which button is which even in bright light. Forget about finding the right button in dim light. Truly horrible design work.

While there are pluses, and it is hitting an attractive price point, I can't see this being worthy of anything more than a little above average (3.5 star) rating. It's a decent, but not exceptional monitor (with a total design failure of a remote). Worth considering if you are looking for a large monitor without breaking the bank, and have moderate expectations as to video quality.
text_fidelity_b: (Discontinued) HP ENVY 32-Inch Screen LED-Lit Monitor Quad-HD

The player is slow. It takes me an average of 30 seconds to a minute from the time I press the power button to the time I can watch the disk that's already in the drive.

The UI is clunky and hard to get used to. Things just don't do what standard UI design suggests they should do. You'll get used to it in time, but it's an unnecessary learning curve.

The UI allows for customization, but it is meaningless. You can't have one person's Hulu account tied to their profile, and a second person's Hulu account tied to their profile. It's just main menu color schemes and the line.

Overall, it's a solid player, and it does everything it needs to do. If you like the features, they are exactly as described. Just be aware of the delay in launching any disks or streaming sources.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic DMP-BDT230 Smart Wi-Fi 3D Blu-Ray Player (2013 Model)

text_fidelity_a:
FiiO X5 High Resolution Music Player (2nd Generation)(Titanium) I love my FiiO X5 2nd gen player! I love that it has two micro SD card slots (which I use both for a total of 192GB of storage space, with one 64GB card and one 128GB card), because I can put two separate sets of music in there and go back and forth between the cards depending on my musical needs (for example, on the 64GB card, I put recently purchased tracks, and for the entirety of my rest of my library, I put those tracks on the 128GB card). It allows me faster access to my newer stuff, which I want to listen to now, vs. randomizing the rest of my music from the other card.

The sound is unheard of (ha ha, sorry for the pun). Nothing compares to the quality of sound that comes out of this little machine, for its size and price. Pair it with a set of high quality hi-fi headphones and some FLAC music files, and you've got yourself an insane little music machine. You'll never go back to Apple or another brand of music player. You'll find yourself hooking it up to your home sound system and playing all of your music through it. I can't say enough for the sound quality. You WILL notice a difference between crummy .mp3 files and other low-quality sound files. You WILL find yourself craving FLAC files, and you will go wherever you can to find them. You might even start converting your entire CD music collection into FLAC, even though you'd already converted them all to .mp3. You WILL find yourself hoping that someday soon, Amazon will start offering FLAC files instead of .mp3s! (HINT HINT NUDGE NUDGE!) ;) Seriously, though, you probably haven't realized how GOOD your music will sound until you listen to it on this FiiO X5 2nd gen. Even the .mp3s sound better. Especially if you use noise cancelling headphones.

I like that you can adjust the configuration and tell it which buttons to remain active when the screen is off, depending on your preferences. I also like that there are several preset themes to choose from. The screen is easy to read and nicely displays album art.

The unit itself has a wonderful weight to it given the aluminum shell. The volume wheel moves easily and there is a slight tactile feedback click. That wheel controls both the song volume and song selection, depending on which screen you're on when you use it. The power on button has a tiny LED light that's blue when it's running and red when it's charging. There are volume up/down buttons beneath the power button and those buttons are some of the buttons that you can choose whether or not to have active while the screen is off.

I'm not sure if I there's a firmware update that needs to be done that could change this, but there are a couple of things that are pretty bothersome in general about this unit:

1) There is no way to search for a song. If, like me, you have more than 5,000 songs, it's impossible to sit and scroll through each album/folder to find a specific song. I suppose if you're some kind of major organization guru (which I thought I was, but apparently not at this), it would be possible to arrange your music folders into genres or some other category to make it easier to get to the exact music you need to play, but if you've moved over from iTunes like I have, you're probably real spoiled with the ability to view songs either by artist, album, song name, etc., as well as the ability to do a search. Here, you're pretty much on your own, depending on how you've got your music library set up. Having purchased most of my music here on Amazon, it's all arranged by artist name in individual folders. I have several hundred folders set up like this, and scrolling through everything with that scroll wheel can take a very, very long time to find the one thing you're looking for.

2) The unit can be quite SLOW to respond to your clicks. It is not touch-screen, and when you click on a button to change tracks forward/backward or to change from looking at what's playing into another option, such as a list of the songs on the album, it can be quite sluggish. Again, if you're used to using an iPod, you'll be frustrated with the lack of responsiveness of this unit. Again, I keep hoping a firmware update will come out that addresses this.

3) Whenever you add music to your micro SD card(s) [NOTE: There is NO onboard storage, it's purely on whatever card(s) you insert into it] you have to completely update your whole media library. This can take a long time depending on how much music you have, so keep this in mind and don't expect to add music and listen to it immediately. In other words, plan ahead for this :)

4) It's not as user friendly as the typical Apple products you may be used to. You'll get used to it, but don't expect the polished feel because of issues like #1 and #2, above.

5) Playlists are not straightforward. Yes, you can be playing a song and add it to a playlist that resides on one of your SD cards. However, importing playlists can be tricky and you may find yourself looking to the internet to help convert your existing playlists from your prior player. Expect to spend some time on this unless you're totally okay with starting over from scratch (I wasn't okay with this). Also, any playlists that you save to your SD card that you've hand-converted do not show up as a playlist on the FiiO. Instead, you have to navigate to the file on your player as if you were looking for a song, and play it as if you were playing a song. Only playlists you've created on the machine show up in the Playlist section, not playlists you've brought in from elsewhere. There is no 'import' feature or anything fancy like that, so you're pretty much on your own unless you add a song one at a time to Playlist 1, Playlist 2, etc. (I do not yet see a way to rename these as there is no keyboard function on this machine, so you're stuck with those names).

I think with time, the FiiO's software will catch up closer to what you're seeing from the high-visibility media consumer based music players, but right now with this X5 you should be more concerned with how WONDERFUL your music sounds vs the issues associated with the frumpy software that comes with it.
text_fidelity_b: FiiO X5 High Resolution Music Player (2nd Generation)(Titanium)

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra Move Style Edition, Black – Wireless Bluetooth Headphones with Superior Sounds Quality, Long Battery Life, Ultra-Light and Comfortable Wireless Headphones, 3.5 mm Jack Connector Included First I like sound! I'm an audiophile at heart but in my life now I'm an audiophile on a BUDGET! These are my first bluetooth speakers. More on that in a minute.

I was looking for on ear bluetooth speakers with a budget of about $50 to $60 and was set on waiting for a sale on the JBL EB45T but then saw these recommended on the wirecutter website (a pretty good review site in my opinion)

There is nothing wrong with these, but nothing really right about them either. They have a nice neutral sound that you can listen to for a long time. For movies and youtube on my computer, they are great. But there is nothing in the sound that is going to wow you either. Trust me if there was something actually wrong with the sound, I'd be telling you. You can listen to these for a long time without ear fatigue. If you are looking for lots of rumble for movies, these probably aren't the right phones for you. But if your movie listening requirements are more modest then these work well for that. For casual background music, podcasts, audiobooks, they will work really well for that.

Isolation is not great. I think the plastic is thin so a certain amount of noise gets in. I wanted to be able to hear a little bit of background noise, things going on in the house, but these push my limit for how much I want to hear. Even though they were open-back my Sennheiser HD-229 did a better job with isolation because of the design of the pad.

Comfort isn't bad and for my ears, the ear cup size is just about right size. I wish the earpieces swiveled a bit more but for my head, they swivel just enough. . They have a left and right and the cups swivel so little that if you have them on the wrong way you will notice.

Bluetooth... These are a pain in the backside on Win 7. When I want to use them I have to go and delete the previous pairing, pair them again and then go to the control panel and set these to be used for output. For movies on the computer, they get out of sync. I even set my movie player (Pot Player which I highly recommend) to use the Bluetooth headphones and they still get out of sync with the audio. I don't know if it's the player, the USB Bluetooth adapter, Windows 7 or some combination of them together.

I like that they can be used with a wire as well as with bluetooth. The controls are a little small, as mentioned by others but I don't have trouble working them.

I also tried the JBL EB45T Bluetooth headphones, which cost almost twice as much, at Target and these sound better overall. The JBL might have had better highs, a little punchier bass but these are more cohesive across the frequency range with nothing tweaked to make them sound 'better'.

Summary: I don't have any other Bluetooth headphones to compare these to but I think most people would be very satisfied with these at this price point for general use. If however, you are looking for audiophile on a budget, it's not here.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Move Style Edition, Black – Wireless Bluetooth Headphones with Superior Sounds Quality, Long Battery Life, Ultra-Light and Comfortable Wireless Headphones, 3.5 mm Jack Connector Included
