text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Sense 2 Advanced Health and Fitness Smartwatch with Tools to Manage Stress and Sleep, ECG App, SpO2, 24/7 Heart Rate and GPS, Shadow Grey/Graphite, One Size (S & L Bands Included) At this point, I have had the Sense 2 for 2 days and I know at least some of my issues will likely be fixed with later software updates. First, the good. I like the form factor. The case is thin and the watch, even with the supplied band, is comfortable. Speaking of the band, as a big guy, I was overjoyed to see the inclusion of a second band that actually fit. Also, changing bands is a snap.

Overall, it seems to be relatively high quality. The battery life, so far at least has been fantastic. I am on hour 42 of wearing it after a 99% charge and it is down to 70% battery left. The screen is fairly bright and crisp. An understated advantage of the Sense 2 (and one of the reasons I switched) is that is OS and phone brand agnostic. You can use it with Apple or Android and, unlike the Galaxy Watch, there are no features locked away if you are not using the correct brand of phone.

If you are coming from a Galaxy Watch where you could customize the watch face and all sorts of other things and that is important to you, then move along. This watch will not be for you. For now, at least, there is not really much substantive you can do to individualize your user experience. That's not so great.

Also not so great is the things that are missing. There is no Google Maps at launch. Also, despite being a Google company, no support for the Google Assistant (Alexa only sadly). There is also no interface to control music on your phone if that is important to you. I found it mildly annoying, but not a deal breaker. In addition, some people will be turned off by the fact that there are features that require a Fitbit paid subscription to get, even though you get six months for free.

The real reason I bought this watch was the ECG function. I have had A Fib for a couple of years and used to use (and still do) a Kardia XL to check my rhythm. The Galaxy Watch 4 was nice because it did a reasonable single lead reading and it meant not having to carry another gizmo with me. You simply held still and put a finger on each of the side buttons. Unfortunately, when I switched from a Galaxy phone to a Pixel, I lost the ability to do an ECG.

On the Sense 2, the ECG has not been impressive. First, I have big hands and contorting my right one to get my thumb and forefinger on the corner of the glass has been a challenge at time. It often takes several tries to get it right. Second, despite confirming on both my Kardia and my Galaxy Watch, the Sense 2 will never indicate that I am in A Fib. Apparently, if your pulse goes above 120 (which mine frequently does while in A Fib) then the Sense 2 just gives up and won't really check. Even in instances where it was below 120, the Sense will not confirm. I guess we get to settle for inconclusive results instead. Given this feature was the main reason I bought the watch, it may be a deal breaker for me and I may return it for that reason. If this feature is not that important to you, then it may still be a good option.

Overall though, it may be a good option for the right person. If you care primarily about health and fitness tracking and want a good battery life, then this is a good option. At the current $300 price point, I still feel like Fitbit may be asking a little too much given the features of the other higher end options on the market.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Sense 2 Advanced Health and Fitness Smartwatch with Tools to Manage Stress and Sleep, ECG App, SpO2, 24/7 Heart Rate and GPS, Shadow Grey/Graphite, One Size (S & L Bands Included)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver) I recently purchased this to replace a lost remote for a piece of high end integrated amp. As with most things in the audiophile world, a replacement for this simple 6 button remote was way overpriced ($105) for what it is. So I was pleased to find that my amplifier was supported by the Logitech 650.

My biggest gripe is nearly a dealbreaker. After setting it up I went to use it on my integrated amplifier to raise the volume a little bit. The problem was that I couldn't just give the volume button a quick tap to turn up the volume a little bit. A quick tap of the volume raised the volume a significant amount whereas the original amp controller allowed me to make volume changes in small increments. After some searching I found that I just had to adjust the IR repeat length in the controller setup.

Problem solved, right? Wrong.

First issue was the manual being outdated. The frustration started when I tried following the steps in the manual. The first step was "Click Troubleshoot at the top of the Harmony Remote Software window". The problem was that there was no Troubleshoot button anymore. They had updated the software but didn't update the manual. Eventually I found the new location in the software where you can lower the repeats. The default was set to 1 so I lowered it to 0 (the lowest setting on the 0-4 scale). I saved my changes and after waiting for the remote to update I tried it again and it still was making large volume changes. With the remote already set to the lowest setting the only way I can make small adjustments to volume is to press the volume button and cover the IR emitter on the remote extremely fast so the volume change signal only gets sent out for a quick burst. I'm talking ninja fast. This is extremely annoying and tricky to get the hang of.

PROS
-Price
-Device Compatibility

CONS
-Can't make small volume changes
-Outdated Manual (they updated the software but didn't update the PDF manual with new instructions for the new software). This causes some serious frustration when you are instructed in Step 1 to press a Troubleshooting button that no longer exists.

Final thoughts... I bought this to mainly do one thing. Change volume and input selection on my integrated amp. The inability to change the volume in small increments is a constant annoyance. It should be something that can be fixed with a software or firmware update.

Logitech, please fix this on the software/firmware side.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin 010-01689-00 Forerunner 35; Easy-to-Use GPS Running Watch, Black I did a good amount of research on other devices before buying this product. I initially wanted a sleek smartwatch that also had great fitness tracking modes, but apparently you either get a pretty smartwatch/OK fitness tracker, or a decent fitness tracker/outdated looking smartwatch. In the end I decided I wanted mainly a fitness tracker that has some smartwatch features, and that I wouldn't use most of the features on an actual smartwatch.

PROS

The app is awesome! My husband is a software developer so I learn a lot about what makes good apps good and what makes bad apps bad. This app is free and user friendly. It has mostly accurate measurements and you can easily track your progress and areas of improvement. It also has a feature that allows whoever you send the link to to track your location, in case you are concerned about getting kidnapped on your run. Very good stuff.

The steps I get seem to be pretty consistent as well as the distance traveled. The heartrate tracker seems to be mostly accurate (checked with manual pulse check).

The battery life is pretty good. Obviously I would use more battery if I am using the fitness modes. Depending on your activity level and use of the fitness modes, the battery could last you all week plus some. The battery charges to full in about 30 minutes.

I like the rectangular watch face and the light green band. I also like that you can change the bands. Apparently for some of the expensive FitBit models the band is not changeable so some people just buy a whole new watch. Like whaaat?

CONS
I like being able to see the texts I get on the watch, but I don't really care for receiving phone calls (I get so many spam calls that I don't even answer my phone lol). I don't think there is a way to say 'no' to having phone calls, so I get frequent notifications to enable phone call permissions. It's not too much of a problem but it's kind of annoying sometimes.

I think the sleep tracker is interesting, but I don't think it is accurate. I think that as long as you are "resting" during the hours that you put as your sleeping hours under Settings, that it considers this as sleep. Sometimes I can't sleep but the device considers this as light sleep. I think this would be an interesting addition, that perhaps it could be integrated: I am a night shift worker and I switch between day/night sleep, so I have to manually enter my bedtimes in the app's User Settings to sleep. I think that if there was an activity button, like when you choose walk/run/cardio on the watch itself, for sleep, it would be easier for me personally. I am not sure if that could be done with a software update or if this is a hardware type thing.

FINAL THOUGHTS

I wear this watch almost 24/7 and I think it has helped me consider and evaluate my activity levels as well as track my improvement. I think that if Garmin made a watch that had the aesthetics and watch interface comparable to the Apple watch but kept the good fitness aspect, I would definitely purchase as an upgrade.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin 010-01689-00 Forerunner 35; Easy-to-Use GPS Running Watch, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech H390 Wired Headset for PC/Laptop, Stereo Headphones with Noise Cancelling Microphone, USB, In-Line Controls, Works with Chromebook - Black I got this headset to practice working with speech recognition software such as Dragon NaturallySpeaking. Overall, I've been surprised and incredibly impressed with the performance. The recognition is better than with the standard headset that came with the software, and the headset does everything I had hoped.

There's a volume control button on the cord, and the USB cord is about 8 feet long, which is plenty generous for connecting to my computer and doing speech recognition.

The only problem with this headset is that I want to use it for hours on end while narrating articles. I'm a freelance writer, and sometimes I either just don't feel like typing, have a sore wrist or fingers, or feel like I can narrate my thoughts faster than I can type them. After about two hours of using this headset, my ears start to ache. I haven't figured out any way of changing the tension on this headset so it doesn't press so hard on my ears.

While I would definitely recommend this headset as a low-budget alternative to higher end products, and for people who would like to use a headset for just an hour or so at a time, I would not recommend it for people who want to use the headset for any kind of professional or serious hobby endeavor. I can see from other reviews that I'm not alone in having my ears hurt, and since I have a small size head, and ears that do not stick out very far, I can only think the problem would be worse for most people than it is for me.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech H390 Wired Headset for PC/Laptop, Stereo Headphones with Noise Cancelling Microphone, USB, In-Line Controls, Works with Chromebook - Black

Sennheiser RS 170 Digital Wireless Headphones (Discontinued By Manufacturer) I have owned these headphones since August, 2014. They are easy to use, and the sound quality is excellent. Prior to owning them, I tried out some $20 wireless headphones from a local drugstore which did not work at all, and I also did a jury-rigged setup with a very long, trip-hazard cable linking some headphones I owned to my TiVo. Never again. Both were a disaster.

This system is absolutely wonderful for two reasons:

First, I have weird hearing issues in that when I am trying to sleep, every little sound bugs me and I seem to hear even a conversation in the next room far more clearly than I have any desire to do, but when listening to TV, I can't understand 75% of what the actors are saying without captions. Go figure. With these headphones, no more problem. All dialog is clear as a bell.

Second, I no longer have to drive my husband crazy blaring the TV in order to adequately hear the actors speaking. By the same token, if my husband is watching a program on TV that I'm not at all interested in, I don't have to be subjected to listening to that either.

It's win-win.

I will say that I was not myself techie enough to install these headphones. My husband is an IT guy and he had to do it for me. So that's one downside for the customer who struggles with techie installations. Other than that, all is great.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony A90J 65 Inch TV: BRAVIA XR OLED 4K Ultra HD Smart Google TV with Dolby Vision HDR and Alexa Compatibility XR65A90J- 2021 Model The box took a big gouge in shipping (in just the original TV box), but the TV was fine, so packaging is probably adequate. Unboxing was easy and there was just a bit of styrofoam and minimal cardboard. Be careful with removing the television from the box, because these things are getting thin enough to be bent under their own weight.

It mounted fine on my old wall mount, but required a different screw size. The screws from my previous setup were the wrong size, so you might want to check what you've got and order some so you don't have to wait around.

There isn't much thought put into cable management, so you'll have to come up with your own solution if you don't want cords visible. Power cord is in the lower right quadrant. Most of the other cords are in the lower left, as is a well hidden power button on the back left. The instructions are minimal. I tried hooking my receiver in as instructed to use the television speaker in place of my old center speaker, but it wouldn't work. It may have just been a clash of brands and standards, because every time I tried to switch to using the TV speakers in the options, it would shut off my Pioneer receiver instead. I ended up using the other speaker input, which did work. I can't believe we're in the 2020's and still cramming bare wires in as audio input. I've got a drawer full of various audio cables here.

Turning it on, I was greeted with setup options. The remote seems high quality, but I wish it had some air-remote functionality. Navigating menus with buttons can get a bit confusing. After getting it hooked up to wifi, I was off to YouTube to find something to make sure it was working right before I hooked everything else up. One of those HD coral reef relaxation videos was just the thing. The picture is vibrant! Bright and colorful. The bezels aren't small enough to tile these together, but are very small. My kids wouldn't let me change the video for hours. They just sat and watched the fish. I'm susceptible to the whine some televisions put out, and I've heard none of that. Worked great for video games, though I didn't try anything especially high end. Worked well for computer output. With the exception of that one audio jack compatibility issue, and the different sized screws, everything has worked as expected.

The screen is a speaker, like a modern smartphone. Sound is good, especially at frequencies you would hear from a center speaker. I definitely still wanted my subwoofer and side speakers to round things out, but it's really nice to have the voices from the television coming from where the faces are, not from some speaker below the television.

I don't have a different brand of 2021 television to compare it to, but my impression is that there is a bit of a premium for the brand name, but it's a very nice product. This was certainly an upgrade for me. A lot of progress has been made in the 8 years since I last upgraded.

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk iXpand 16GB Mobile Flash Drive with Lightning Connector for iPhones, iPads & Computers (SDIX-016G-G57) I bought this because I was traveling abroad and I wanted to backup my phone pictures. If my phone got lost or stolen on the last day of the trip, I would lose all my pictures from the entire trip. It's definitely better to backup your pictures each evening so they most you could ever lose would be the pictures from 1 day. You would still have the rest.

This is mostly just an issue when traveling abroad. Back home where WiFi is common, the iCloud backup is just fine. Unless you take zillions of pictures, you can even use your cell data to backup your pictures when there's no WiFi (assuming you have a reasonable data plan). However, when traveling abroad or on a cruise, access to the cloud can be quite expensive and/or limited. That's where this device comes in handy. Backup your pictures without WiFi or cell data.

There is another reason why you might want this device. If you take tons of pictures on your phone, then space can be a problem. You might be running out of space on your phone and/or the cloud. Or maybe you don't have an iCloud account at all. You want to make room on your phone, but you also want to keep all the pictures. You can copy your pictures to this device, and delete them off the phone to make room for more pictures.

The concept of backup up pictures from your phone is a good one, but I don't think this device is the best way to do it. I just bought the RAVPower FileHub wireless travel router, SD card reader, USB portable drive companion. I think that's going to end up being a better solution than this device.

There are a couple of things I don't like about this device:
1) The drive is very wide. If you have two USB ports that are close to each other, the drive will block the other port.
2) I find the connection to the iPhone to be awkward. The lightning connector on the device is on the end of this flexible rubber arm on the side of the device. You bend this arm away from the device (but not too far, per the warning in the instructions), and plug it into the phone. It's hard to describe, but you end up with this thing at an awkward angle hanging off the bottom of the phone. You wouldn't want to put it in your pocket like that, and it sits funny on the table since both the phone and the device are at an angle. If you flip the device around, you can get the phone to lay flat on the table, but then the device is blocking the home button. It's a really goofy design.
3) This last one takes a while to explain. There is a sync mode, where you can automatically sync the device with your phone. This will save any new pictures from your phone onto the drive. Here's how it works: You run the app, plug the device into the lightning connector, and run the sync. Pictures are copied to a folder on the drive that you specify. Since you create the folder originally, and you associate the phone's sync with that folder, you can use the device with multiple phones. Simply use a different folder for each phone. When you sync, any new pictures on the phone which aren't already in the sync folder will be copied to the drive. The concept is very good.

However, one huge drawback of the sync is that the file named aren't preserved. For example, if you just copy a picture off your phone using some other method, you'll get something like "IMG_2841". That's an easy name to deal with, if you want to do something with a particular picture (e.g. Bob wants a copy of IMG_1531, or I want to print an 8x10 of IMG_2316).

Unfortunately, when you use the sync method, the file names are not preserved. The picture files get really long names with a seemingly random string of characters. I'm sure the names mean something to the sync program, but for a human they just look like random garbage. In any case, your drive ends up with this sync folder filled with hundreds (or thousands) of files with random unreadable names. If you want to do anything with the files, you'll wish they had more recognizable names.

Let's say for example that you copied IMG_1000 and IMG_1001 off your phone using some other method, and later you decide you also want IMG_1002. Well, you know that the picture must be in the sync folder, but good luck finding it. You wish you could just sort by name and grab IMG_1002 directly, but since the names are all random you'll need to scroll through hundreds (or thousands) of thumbnails and try to figure out which picture was originally called IMG_1002.

Because of this issue, I think the sync mode is useless.

However, you can still back up your pictures in a semi-manual way. The trick is that if you do a manual copy to get a picture from the phone onto the drive, then the original file name is preserved. So, instead of doing the sync, use the manual copy mode. This isn't quite as tedious as it sounds because the app understands the problem with duplicate file names, and it gives you the opportunity to deal with them.

Here's what you do. Set up a folder on the drive where you want to backup your phone's pictures. Using the app, select all the pictures on the phone and copy them to this folder. Let's say you have 500 pictures. The copy will take a while, but you will eventually have all 500 pictures in that folder on the drive. Then a few days later, you want to backup your newer pictures, but you aren't sure exactly which ones are new. Do the same thing you did originally. Using the app, select all the pictures on the phone, and tell the app to copy them to that same folder. After thinking about it for a while, it will tell you that you have selected 541 pictures to copy, but 500 of them have duplicate file names. It will ask you what you want to do about that. Select the "skip" option, and any file with a duplicate file name won't get copied. In this example, it will only copy the 41 pictures that weren't there before.

This works, but it's still not great. It takes a while to analyze the files before starting the copy. Let's say you had 1000 pictures originally, and you only took 2 new ones. The backup should be fast, right? Well, no. It takes the app a surprisingly long time to analyze the 1002 pictures and figure out that 1000 of them have duplicate file names. Eventually, it will tell you about the 1000 duplicates and you can select "skip". Then it will copy only the 2 new pictures. But even though there were only two new pictures, the process takes a frustratingly long time.

If you know exactly which pictures are new, and there aren't very many, you can always just pick those by hand instead of doing the select-all. In that case, the process is very fast since the app is only dealing with the few pictures you selected and not analyzing a 1000 of them.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk iXpand 16GB Mobile Flash Drive with Lightning Connector for iPhones, iPads & Computers (SDIX-016G-G57)
